title: VfL Bochum — Grokipedia
content: Bundesliga as of the 2025/26 season.](#ref-1) The club traces its origins to July 26, 1848, when it was established as a gymnastics association following a call in the local newspaper *Märkischer Sprecher*, making it one of the oldest sports organizations in the world.](#ref-2) The football department was formed in 1938 through a merger of local teams, and the current independent football entity, Verein für Leibesübungen Bochum 1848 Fußballgemeinschaft, was officially founded on July 29, 1949, while retaining the historic 1848 designation.](#ref-3) With approximately 30,000 members, VfL Bochum embodies the industrial spirit of the Ruhr region and has a reputation as a resilient "yo-yo club," frequently moving between the top two tiers of German football since its inaugural promotion to the Bundesliga in 1971.](#ref-3) The club's home matches are played at the Vonovia Ruhrstadion, a historic venue opened in 1911 with a current capacity of 27,599 spectators.](#ref-4) Over its history, VfL Bochum has achieved notable success in cup competitions, including runner-up finishes in the DFB-Pokal in 1968 and 1988, as well as winning the Western German Cup in 1968.](#ref-5) In European competition, its greatest accomplishment was reaching the semi-finals of the 1981/82 UEFA Cup. Domestically, the team has recorded its best Bundesliga finishes of fifth place in the 1996/97 and 2003/04 seasons, and it has secured multiple promotions, including a dramatic penalty shootout victory in the 2023/24 relegation playoff to avoid demotion before ultimately finishing 18th in the 2024/25 Bundesliga and relegating to the second division.](#ref-2)](#ref-6) Despite lacking major titles, VfL Bochum's enduring presence in professional football highlights its role as a symbol of perseverance for its passionate fanbase in the working-class Ruhr area.](#ref-4).

title: VfL Bochum - Wikipedia
content: # VfL Bochum. **Verein für Leibesübungen Bochum 1848 Fußballgemeinschaft**, commonly referred to as **VfL Bochum** (German pronunciation:  ⓘ), is a German professional association football club based in the city of Bochum, North Rhine-Westphalia. Following World War II, the football section resumed play as the independent **VfL Bochum 1848** and played its first season in the second division 2. With the formation of the Bundesliga, Germany's new professional league, in 1963 VfL found itself in the third tier Amateurliga Westfalen.*[citation needed*] A first-place result there in 1965 raised them to the Regionalliga West (II),*[citation needed*] from which they began a steady climb up the league table to the Bundesliga in 1971.*[citation needed*] During this rise, Bochum also played its way to the final of the 1967–68 DFB-Pokal, where they lost 1–4 to 1. The club made a repeat appearance in the DFB-Pokal final in 1988, losing 1–0 to Eintracht Frankfurt.*[citation needed*] Relegated after a 16th-place finish in the 1992–93 season, the team became a classic "yo-yo club",*[according to whom?*] moving between the Bundesliga and 2.
